newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche BA targets Lufthansa with new fares.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche BA targets Lufthansa with new fares.

text.p: Deutsche BA, the airline 49 percent-owned by British Airways Plc, stepped up competition in Germany to market-leader Deutsche Lufthansa AG on Monday with a range of new fares and new domestic routes.

Deutsche BA said new standard return fares for its domestic flights would range from 190 marks to 520 marks, depending on booking options. The airline said it would from Monday be flying the Munich-Hamburg and Munich-Cologne/Bonn routes.
A one-off "Valentine fare" will also be offered around Valentine's Day next month that will see internal flight fares drop to 99 marks at that time, Deutsche BA said in a statement.

The launch of the new fares and routes comes a week after Lufthansa was warned by the German Federal Cartel Office for charging too much for its Frankfurt-Berlin run, a route that Deutsche BA currently does not have access to.

Lufthansa refuted the criticism that it was charging too much for this and other domestic routes, arguing that the routes were not even profit-making, and that any airline undercutting its prices would sustain higher losses.

Deutsche BA in a statement said that it was expecting to increase its 1996/97 turnover to 550 million marks, compared to 492 million the year before, and that it expected to be profitable in two years.
It added that it carried some 1.23 million passengers in the six months to September 30, 1996, compared to 1.15 million in the comparable period of the year before.
Outside BA's 49 percent stake, Deutsche BA shares are held by three banks, which will have the option to sell their stakes at some point this summer.
